reader.requirement: At --std 85, when a USE statement names file-name-1 explicitly, no other USE statement (OUTPUT or EXTEND mode-scoped) may apply to that file. Its exceptions, on a report file or any other organization, in output or extend mode, select only the file-name declarative, including when it is reached as a container's GLOBAL declarative.

reader.edition-search: Grepped the same emitters and ProcedureTableBuilder for DialectBehavior, DialectLevel, CobolVersion and .Edition. EmitScopeTiers always emits the file-name switch before the open-mode switch, and each case returns, so a file-name match ends the selection at every edition.

reader.notes: Within one Procedure Division and on the outward GLOBAL walk, the file-name tier always wins. One doubt: in PI2 the nested program's own USE ON EXTEND runs for the GLOBAL file F that the container names in a USE GLOBAL. That follows the IPC precedence (§1985:X.5.5.4 GR1a) and the reading that GR4 and GR5c are scoped to one Procedure Division (2023 says so explicitly in GR5). A literal run-unit-wide reading of GR4 would instead select OUTER-F.

refuter.evidence: Probe E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-153/src/r4globr2.cob (run runs/r4globr2-001, --std 85): container PO declares report file RFL GLOBAL, a non-GLOBAL USE AFTER ERROR ON RFL and a USE GLOBAL AFTER ERROR ON EXTEND; nested PI1 runs OPEN EXTEND RFL (absent, 35). Printed: '1 OUTER OPEN EXTEND RFL / OUTER-RF-LOCAL 35 / 2 CALL PI1 / OUTER-GLOBAL-EXTEND 35 / PI1 RFL 35'. The container's EXTEND declarative ran for RFL although the same Procedure Division names RFL explicitly in a USE. Same with a sequential GLOBAL file (r4glob.cob, runs/r4glob-001; a never-named file G correctly reaches OUTER-GLOBAL-EXTEND). Same output at --std 2023 (r4globr2-002, r4glob-002). Cause in code: UseTierEmitter.EmitScopeTiers with globalOnly:true filters the non-GLOBAL file-name declaratives out BEFORE the file-name tier, so the mode tier no longer excludes the files those USEs name. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR4 ... the text is in GR4' ("When file-name-1 is specified explicitly, no other USE statement applies to file-name-1."); 'OK  §1985:XIII.4.8.4 GR5c ... the text is in GR5c' ("except those files referenced by file-name-1 in another USE statement specifying the same condition"); 'OK  §1985:X.5.5.4 GR1 ... the text is in GR1' ("The declarative which is selected for execution must satisfy the rules for execution of that declarative"). The reader's probes never combined a non-GLOBAL file-name USE with a GLOBAL mode USE in one container. kb/Work: no note found (grep of 'no other USE', 'XIII.4.8.4', 'globalOnly').
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Compiler/CodeGen/UseTierEmitter.cs#EmitScopeTiers: globalOnly drops non-GLOBAL file-name USEs before the file-name exclusion is applied (not an edition switch, but the arm the outward walk takes)
refuter.corrected: NON-CONFORMING (wrong-answer, cause b: the same at --std 2023). At 85 a file named explicitly in any USE of a Procedure Division is excluded from that Procedure Division's OUTPUT/EXTEND declaratives (GR4, GR5b/c), and X.5.5.4 GR1 selects only a declarative that satisfies its own execution rules; so for PI1's failing OPEN EXTEND RFL the container's USE GLOBAL ON EXTEND does not apply and, with no other qualifying GLOBAL declarative, none is executed. The compiler runs OUTER-GLOBAL-EXTEND. Reading stated: GR4/GR5c are scoped at least to the Procedure Division holding both USE statements (the narrowest reading of the text); the non-GLOBAL USE's invisibility to PI1 does not lift the exclusion, because the exclusion is a property of the EXTEND USE statement, not of the file-name declarative's reach.

adjudication.reason: The mechanism of kb/Work PB5821 in the report module: a container's USE GLOBAL ... ON OUTPUT runs for a file its own non-GLOBAL USE names.
